newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas still up sharply on weather.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas still up sharply on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained sharply higher in moderate, late trade Monday, still driven by forecasts for some Arctic-like U.S. temperatures later this week and next, industry sources said.
At 1400 EST, February was still up by 52.4 cents at $3.63 per million British thermal units, while March was 45.6 cents higher at $3.25. Most others were up by one to 15 cents.

"The resurgence of (cold) weather helped get the market up and running again. We had a healthy correction, but now I think we'll hang up here for a while," said one Midwest trader, noting cold weather already had hit that region.
Forecasters are calling for well below-normal Midwest temperatures this week, with the cold expected to dip into Texas later this week. Eastern temperatures were expected to dive by late week.
Technically, traders now pegged February resistance in the $3.90s and then at the contract high of $4.02. Support was seen in the $2.60s.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices jumped almost 90 cents Monday to the $3.45 to $3.50 area. Midcon pipes surged more than $1.30 on the cold to the $3.65-3.70 range. Gas at the New York city gate gained 50 cents to about $4.00.
NYMEX said 36,546 Hub contracts traded at 1330 EST. Open interest on Jan 3 rose 1,247 contracts to 147,975.
NYMEX Alberta natgas was still untraded at 1400 EST. NYMEX March Permian natgas traded once at a new high of $2.55, up 20 cents. Other months remained untraded.

On the KCBT, February gained 55 cents to $3.45, while March was 54 cents higher at $3.11, a new high. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.6 cents to 18.0 cents (NYMEX premium). Separately, Enron said its gas compressor station in South Dakota on the Northern Border pipeline, shut over the weekend to repair a valve, was now back in service.
